DSH Web Guard

A password gate for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI —
one plugin that fixes four deployment problems at
once and adds a native settings page.
中文说明
| Problem | Vanilla behaviour | dsh-web-guard |
| No human login | A per-process `?token=` printed to the terminal, new on every restart | One passw

ord + revocable sessions |
| `/api` returns 403 behind a proxy | The browser-trust fence requires `H
ost` to arrive unrewritten; NPM/Caddy rewrite it | The proxy rewrites `Host`/`Origin` to the loopbac

k authority, which the fence accepts |
| Token lives in the journal | `journalctl \| grep token` bef

ore you can get in | Exchanged in-process; the browser never sees a token |
| UI breaks on plain HTT
P | `crypto.randomUUID is not a function` outside a secure context | Injects a `getRandomValues` pol
ypto.randomUUID is not a function` outside a secure context | Injects a `getRandomValues` polyfill |
Zero runtime dependencies (Node standard library only). The npm package ships prebuilt JavaScript, s
o `dsh plugin add` needs no toolchain; building from a checkout is a maintainer command (`npm run bu
plugin add` needs no toolchain; building from a checkout is a maintainer command (`npm run build`).
Requires **DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` or newer** (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`). On an inco
mpatible host the whole bundle is skipped — for a front door that means the gate does not start, so
upgrade DSH rather than removing the plugin.
## Screenshots
Login page  ·  sign-out confirmation  ·  native DSH Web Guard page in the harness settings (follows
the harness light/dark theme)
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The harness fence accepts a loopback authority, so making every upstream request look like one remov
es the 403 entirely. Authentication happens **in the proxy**, not as a front-end overlay — a request
without a session cookie never reaches the harness.
A small browser half (`dsh.client`) adds the management page to the harness Settings panel; the gate
itself is entirely server-side and keeps working if the browser half cannot load.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`main` only ever carries released code (development happens on `dev`), so this
installs the latest s

table release. Installing is enough — the package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the guard row is
mounted
automatically. Restart `dsh`.

**On first start a password is generated**, printed to the terminal and stored
(hashed) in `<profile

>/data/dsh-web-guard.json` with mode `0600`. To pin your own,
add a row to `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cord

is.patch.yml` (it overrides the bundle
defaults):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Note that a profile patch replaces the whole `config` object, so restate every
key you care about.
**Upgrading from v2:** the bottom-right shield button and `/__guard/admin` are gone; management live
s in **Settings → DSH Web Guard**. Reinstall the package (or update to `3.0.0`) and restart DSH. The
password hash, session cache and settings file keep their format, so nobody is signed out and your
configuration carries over.
> The harness itself must listen on loopback (its default). If it is bound to a LAN address, clients
can bypass the gate by connecting there directly — the plugin detects this at startup and warns.
## ⚠️ This is the front door, not an optional plugin
Once installed, **dsh-web-guard is the only way in**: it listens on 3081 and forwards to a DSH that
is bound to loopback only (3080). If the plugin stops loading, 3081 stops listening and **both your
LAN and the internet lose access at once** — while DSH itself keeps running, with your sessions and
data intact. That is the dangerous shape: the door is welded shut and you are standing outside it.
**If you exposed this address to the internet, take this seriously.**
Three rules:
1. **Do not uninstall it and do not disable it.** Concretely: don't run `dsh plugin --profile web re
move @lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard`, don't drop the entry from `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `p

ackage.json`, and don't add `disabled: true` to it in `cordis.patch.yml`.
2. **DSH's Settings → Plug
ins page is a read-only inventory** — status tags only (enabled / disabled / failed), no toggles. Do

n't go looking for an off switch there; accidents happen on the command line instead.
3. Upgrading,
editing config and `systemctl restart dsh-web` are all safe. Only "making it not load" is not.
### If you closed it by accident
Relax: **DSH is still running on `127.0.0.1:3080`; sessions, workspace and password are all intact.*
* Only the gate is gone. Recovery takes two commands and **does not depend on the plugin being loade

## Security model
- Passwords are hashed with scrypt (random salt). The plaintext appears exactly once, in the generat

ed-password log line.
- Session tokens are stored server-side as SHA-256 digests; cookies are `HttpO

nly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when TLS is on.
- Login POSTs are checked for a same-hostname `Or

igin`. The session cookie's `SameSite` attribute is the primary CSRF defence.
- Repeated failures fr

om one IP trigger a temporary lock (in-memory, cleared on restart).
- **The session table is cached
on disk** (`<profile>/data/dsh-web-guard-sessions-<port>.json`, mode `0600`, atomic tmp+rename), so
**restarting DSH no longer signs signed-in browsers out**. The file holds SHA-256 digests, never tok
ens — neither the cache nor a heap dump can mint a working cookie. The filename carries the listener

port, so a shadow instance cannot overwrite the live one.
- `/logout` ends the current browser sess
ion. To revoke everything (a suspected leak, say), use the settings page's **sign out all devices**
— **a restart is not a revocation any more**.
**This is not multi-user.** One password, one privilege level. The harness agent can execute code, s
o anyone who gets in has code execution on that host — which is the product's design, not a bug in t
who gets in has code execution on that host — which is the product's design, not a bug in the gate.
